node.title: Re: read database 500 error
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
But for some reason the script keeps popping a 500 error and there is nothing in my log files.

When running a script as a CGI script, it needs to output headers before anything else. Please see one of the [id://11132949|alternatives to CGI.pm] for which modules you could use. As one example, you might try:

use CGI::Simple; my $q = CGI::Simple->new; print $q->header();

In general, [id://111088], and see also [id://745674], [id://165253], and [id://380424]. Note you can always run your CGI script from the command line first to see any errors.

Update: Also, note print ("--", @row), " "; is not doing what you think, and [doc://warnings] would have given you some hints about that: it's being interpreted as ( print("--", @row), " " ); - that is, [doc://print] is only getting the arguments "--", @row, but not " ". You need to write print "--", @row, " "; or print(("--", @row), " "); instead. And it's best not to use $a and $b as variable names as those get special treatment by [doc://sort].
